Subject: Administrator can Authenticate
Description:
As an administrator, I want to sign in using my provisioned account so I can access administration functions for my association.

\- An active administrator account and association membership exist; its password is stored only as a salted password hash.  
\- Valid credentials authenticate the administrator through the shared login endpoint; the system derives the correct association role.  
\- Incorrect credentials, nonexistent accounts and globally inactive accounts receive the same generic 401 response.  
\- Anonymous callers cannot use protected endpoints; authenticated callers cannot access another association without membership.  
\- Authentication responses expose no password, hash or unrelated profile data. Enforce the agreed expiry, abuse limits and browser protection rules.  
\- Evidence: S1-62 tests, implementation tasks #73–#78 and the shared #83/#86 policy/test work.

Subject: Administrator can create users
Description:
As an association administrator, I want to create resident accounts so approved people can access our association.

- Only a caller with active admin membership in the target association can create an account; resident callers receive 403 and inaccessible associations receive 404.
- Validate `displayName`, `email`, `temporaryPassword` and `confirmPassword` against the shared rules. Do not accept a role field.
- Canonical email is globally unique. Duplicate email returns 409 with the agreed safe error body and no partial records.
- Store only a salted password hash; atomically create the user and active resident membership.
- Success returns 201 with a safe user DTO and confirmation in the interface. Temporary credentials are handled privately and are never logged or returned in a toast.
- Under the documented onboarding contract, a new account must change its temporary password before business access. Link the first-login implementation under #64.
- User listing and access-state management are deferred until after the internship; scheduling is to be decided.

Subject: Registered user can authenticate
Description:
As a registered user, I want to sign in with my administrator-created account so I can securely access the functions permitted to me.

\- Use the same login endpoint as administrators. Valid credentials advance through any required first-login password change and then allow identity loading.  
\- Incorrect credentials, nonexistent accounts and globally inactive accounts receive generic 401 responses.  
\- A globally active account may authenticate with zero active association memberships, but receives no association access. Disabling one membership denies that association without disabling unrelated memberships.  
\- GET identity returns only the caller's profile and active memberships. Server policies reject resident calls to admin functions and reject cross-association access.  
\- Valid authentication persists across protected navigation and page reload within the agreed expiry. Logout/expiry prevents credential reuse and clears protected frontend state.  
\- Display field/credential/network errors and prevent duplicate submissions according to the UI criteria.  
\- Evidence: S1-64-01–08, shared S1-62 authentication/password criteria, tasks #83–#86 and first-login tasks if not already implemented. Profile editing is deferred until after the internship; scheduling is to be decided.

Subject: [FE] Shared CSRF API Client, Auth Bootstrap & Session Teardown
Description:
## Context & Anti-Hallucination Rules (READ FIRST)
- **DO NOT** invent `/api/associations/...` routes. Those are obsolete.
- **DO NOT** store session tokens, user roles, or passwords in `localStorage` or `sessionStorage`.
- Follow Task 8 of `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-23-resident-administration-crud.md` and `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-23-resident-administration-crud-design.md`.

## Files to Create / Modify

- Modify: `frontend/src/auth/auth.ts`
- Modify: `frontend/src/App.tsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/pages/IssueLayout.tsx`
- Modify: `frontend/src/pages/Dashboard.tsx`

## Exact Implementation Requirements
1. **Shared API Client (`frontend/src/api/client.ts`):**
   - Implement **Singleton Interceptor Pattern** (`apiRequest<T>(path, options)`).
   - Keep CSRF token in module memory only (`let csrfToken: string | null = null`).
   - Before any `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH`, or `DELETE`, fetch `GET /api/auth/csrf` if `csrfToken` is null, and attach `X-CSRF-TOKEN: <token>` header.
   - Always send `credentials: "same-origin"` and `Content-Type: "application/json"` (when body is present).
   - If the backend responds with `403` and `error.code === "CSRF_INVALID"`, clear the cached CSRF token, fetch a fresh one from `GET /api/auth/csrf`, and retry the request **once**.
   - Decode non-2xx responses into a typed `ApiError { status, code, message, fields }`.
2. **Replace Mock Auth (`frontend/src/auth/auth.ts`):**
   - Delete `USERS_KEY`, `SESSION_KEY`, `PENDING_USER_KEY`, `initialUsers`, and all `localStorage` calls.
   - Implement `getIdentity(): Promise<SessionUser | null>` calling `GET /api/auth/me` (returns `{ id, name, email, role: "admin" | "resident", mustChangePassword }`; returns `null` on `401`).
   - Implement `login(email, password)` calling `POST /api/auth/login` (`{ email, password }` -> `{ next: "app" | "change_password" }`).
   - Implement `changePassword(newPassword, confirmPassword)` calling `POST /api/auth/change-password` (`{ newPassword, confirmPassword }` -> `{ next: "app" }`).
   - Implement `signOut()` calling `POST /api/auth/logout` with `{}` body and CSRF header, clearing in-memory identity.
3. **Async Bootstrap & Route Guards (`frontend/src/App.tsx`, `IssueLayout.tsx`):**
   - On mount in `App.tsx`, call `getIdentity()`. Render a clean loading state while resolving (no flash of protected content).
   - If unauthenticated (`null`), render `<LoginPage />`.
   - If `user.mustChangePassword === true`, force render `<ChangePassword />` regardless of URL path.
   - Make `handleSignOut` in `IssueLayout.tsx` and `Dashboard.tsx` `async` so it awaits `signOut()` before redirecting to `/`.

Subject: [BE] Scoped Issues API Endpoints & State Transition Service
Description:
## Context & Anti-Hallucination Rules (READ FIRST)

- Implements the backend for Story `#95` (Administrator Incident Triage & Resolution Workflow) and Story `#93` (Resident Incident Reporting & My Issues Flow).
- The EF Core entities `Issue` (`backend/src/Locatarius.Domain/Entities/Issue.cs`) and `IssueAttachment` already exist in PostgreSQL (`issues` and `issue_attachments` tables), and `DemoDataSeeder.cs` already seeds demo issues.
- **DO NOT** create a new database migration unless strictly needed. Use the existing `LocatariusDbContext.Issues` set!
- **Security / IDOR Isolation Rule:**
  - An **Admin** (`UserRoleType.Admin`) can ONLY list, view, or update issues where `issue.Building.AdminId == adminUserId`.
  - A **Resident** (`UserRoleType.Resident`) can ONLY list or view issues for their assigned building (`issue.BuildingId == user.Apartment.BuildingId`) and create issues for their own assigned apartment's building (`ReportedBy` is ALWAYS set from `authorization.User.UserId` on the server, never trusted from JSON).
  - Any request for an `issueId` outside the caller's building scope MUST return `404 NOT_FOUND` (`ApiErrors.NotFound("ISSUE_NOT_FOUND", "Issue not found.")`).

## Files to Create / Modify

- Create: `backend/src/Locatarius.Infrastructure/Issues/IssueService.cs`
- Create: `backend/src/Locatarius.Api/Validation/IssueRequestValidator.cs`
- Create: `backend/src/Locatarius.Api/Controllers/IssuesController.cs`
- Modify: `backend/src/Locatarius.Api/Program.cs` (register `IssueService`)
- Create: `backend/tests/Locatarius.Infrastructure.Tests/IssuesHttpTests.cs`

## Exact Implementation Requirements

1. **Endpoints in `IssuesController` (`[Route("api/issues")]`):**
   - Authorize all endpoints via `SessionAuthorizationService.AuthorizeAsync(..., SessionType.Full, requireAdmin: ...)`.
   - Validate CSRF (`IAntiforgery`) and 16 KiB body limit on all `POST` / `PATCH` routes.
   - `GET /api/issues`: Returns scoped list of `IssueDto` ordered by `CreatedAt` descending.
     - `IssueDto` shape matching `frontend/src/features/issue-triage/issueModel.ts`: `{ issueId, reportedBy, buildingId, buildingNumber, title, description, status: (1|2|3), priority: (1|2|3|4), createdAt, updatedAt, resolvedAt, reporter: { userId, firstName, lastName, apartment: { apartmentNumber } | null }, attachments: [...] }`.
   - `GET /api/issues/{id:guid}`: Returns single scoped `IssueDto` or `404`.
   - `POST /api/issues` (Resident only; Admin returns `403`): Accepts `{ title, description, priority? }`. Validates `title` (5–120 chars, no control chars) and `description` (10–2000 chars). Requires caller to have a non-null `ApartmentId` (`400` or `404` if unassigned). Sets `ReportedBy = user.UserId`, `BuildingId = user.Apartment.BuildingId`, `Status = IssueStatus.Open`, `CreatedAt = UtcNow`. Returns `201 Created`.
   - `PATCH /api/issues/{id:guid}` (Admin only; Resident returns `403`): Accepts `{ status?, priority? }`. Locks or verifies building ownership (`issue.Building.AdminId == adminId`), updates `Status` (`1=Open`, `2=InProgress`, `3=Resolved`), sets `UpdatedAt = UtcNow`, sets `ResolvedAt = UtcNow` when `Status == Resolved` (or `null` if reopened), and updates `Priority` if not Resolved. Returns `200 OK` with updated `IssueDto`.
2. **Integration Tests (`IssuesHttpTests.cs`):**
   - Verify Resident A can create and list issues in Building A, cannot see Building B issues (`404`), and gets `403` calling `PATCH /api/issues/{id}`.
   - Verify Admin A can triage/update Building A issues and gets `404` on Admin B's issues.
